firmwareNotes: Chart valid for OS 2.5 per TE's EP-133 guide ver 2.5 (system: 14.1 midi reference, 14.2 note map, 14.5 cc map). OS 2.5 released 2026-06-24; latest 2.5.1 (2026-07-03, USB-audio fix only). CC 12/13/64, USB audio, and identity over TRS need OS >= 2.5. Earlier OS: only CC 1 + bank select. OS 2.0 (2025-04-09) added system MIDI in/out channels, MIDI thru, per-pad MIDI-in channel, pitch bend/mod wheel input, and program change. OS 2.0.1 added setting 127. Since OS 2.0.2 program change is no longer mapped (recorded/relayed only). The identity reply's version bytes are zero on 2.5.x, so read the OS version on the device.

usb.notes: Driverless USB-MIDI device (TE's own browser EP Sample Tool talks to it over Web MIDI). USB-C is a device port, not a MIDI host. macOS MIDI input and output are both named 'EP-133' (ko-bridge, mcp-koii). USB audio (OS >= 2.5, docs: works with any class-compliant USB audio host, stereo in/out): CoreAudio device 'EP-133', 2 in / 2 out at 48 kHz (engine runs at 46.875 kHz), so Chrome getUserMedia can capture it. Disable echoCancellation/noiseSuppression/autoGainControl. Measured MIDI note to USB audio about 3.6 ms. Close TE's EP Sample Tool tab while the demo app runs (the device allows one SysEx file session).

identity.notes: TE implementation chart: SysEx = 'identity request+reply, proprietary messages' (docs). OS 2.5 notes: identity now also works over TRS MIDI. Reply bytes captured over USB on OS 2.5.x (ko-bridge, 2026-10-16): device-ID byte 0x33 (EP-133 product code, not 7F), manufacturer 00 20 76, family 20 00 (LSB-first = 0x0020 = 32, consistent with SKU TE032AS00x), member 02 00, software version 00 00 00 00 (zeroed on 2.5.x, verified by ep-series-sysex). Parse by position: bytes[1]=7E, [3..4]=06 02, [5..7]=00 20 76. Do not filter on the device-ID byte. EP-40 uses product byte 0x3C. TE proprietary SysEx = F0 00 20 76 33 40 <flags> <reqId> <cmd> ... F7 (GREET 0x01, FILE 0x05, DFU). Not needed for control. Chrome needs requestMIDIAccess({sysex:true}).

channels.receive: Default (system setting 110): receive on ALL channels. Setting 111-126 = receive and send only on channel 1-16. Setting 127 = pads only send and receive when a MIDI channel is assigned in SOUND EDIT. Per pad (OS >= 2.0): SHIFT+SOUND > (-/+ to the MIDI page) > knob X = channel (send and receive), knob Y = root note. No per-group (A-D) channel setting: groups are addressed by note range.
channels.send: Pad presses/sequenced notes go out on channel 1 by default (system channel; ko-bridge observed ch 1), or on a pad's own sound-edit channel. Device sends CC 120 on stop (community). Clock out only with setting 102. No documented CC output from knobs or fader.
channels.notes: System settings: SHIFT+ERASE, type the 3-digit code (applies immediately; ko-bridge also pressed MAIN). Not settable over SysEx or MIDI. With default omni, any note 36-83 on any channel fires a pad. For a melodic pad on ch 2, either keep pitched notes below 36 or set system code 111 (ch 1 only).

notes.description: Notes 36-83 trigger the 48 pads: group A = 36-47, B = 48-59, C = 60-71, D = 72-83. Within a group the order is '.', '0', 'enter', '1'..'9' (keypad bottom-left to top-right). In KEYS mode, notes 0-127 play the selected pad chromatically. A pad with its own MIDI channel plays at pitch on that channel.

parameters.name: Trigger pad (groups A-D)
parameters.channel: default: any channel (system 110 = receive all, send ch 1). Send on ch 1.
parameters.notes: Note On 0x9n, velocity 0-127 recognised. note = 36 + 12*group(A=0..D=3) + padIndex; padIndex order: '.',0,enter,1..9 (bottom-left to top-right). Hardware-verified by several community tools. Velocity-0 note-on is handled as note-off (OS 1.1.1). Send matching Note Offs: KEY/LEGATO pads play while held (ONESHOT pads likely ignore note-off, inferred).

parameters.name: Play a pad chromatically (per-pad channel)
parameters.channel: the channel assigned to that pad in SOUND EDIT > MIDI (knob X)
parameters.notes: OS >= 2.0: a pad's sound-edit MIDI channel is also its MIDI-in channel. Notes on that channel play the pad's sample at pitch, relative to the pad root note (knob Y). Community-verified (C1-G1 on ch 2 played a bass pad at pitch). In KEYS mode on the device, incoming notes 0-127 play the selected pad chromatically.

parameters.name: Pitch bend
parameters.notes: OS 2.0 notes: incoming pitch bend affects sample playback. Bend range not documented. Centre = 8192.

parameters.name: Vibrato (mod wheel)
parameters.notes: TE CC map prints range 1-127. OS 2.0: mod wheel affects sample playback (vibrato). Subtle; best on a sustained KEY/LEGATO pad.

parameters.name: FX parameter X (master FX knob X)
parameters.notes: OS >= 2.5. Controls knob X of the currently selected FX: delay time, reverb length, distortion drive, chorus modulation, filter cutoff (left = low-pass, right = high-pass), or compressor drive. Audible only if an FX type is selected and a group's FX send (fader in FX mode) is up. Community warning: one OS 2.5 hardware test (mcp-koii) heard no audible change sweeping CC 12/13 on ch 1, cause unknown. midi.guide describes it as the selected punch-in effect's X. Verify before going on camera.

parameters.name: FX parameter Y (master FX knob Y)
parameters.notes: OS >= 2.5. Knob Y of the selected FX: delay feedback, reverb color, distortion color, chorus feedback, filter resonance, compressor speed. Same caveats as CC 12.

parameters.name: Sustain pedal
parameters.notes: OS >= 2.5. Sustains KEY and LEGATO sound modes only (not oneshot). >=64 = down, <64 = up.

parameters.name: All sound off / all notes off (panic)
parameters.notes: TE implementation chart lists all sound off (CC 120), reset all controllers (121) and all notes off (123) under channel-mode messages, but the received/transmitted marks were not readable. The device itself sends CC 120 on stop (community). Use CC 120 then CC 123 as panic.

notControllableViaMidi: Per-sound volume (AMP), pitch (PTC), pan, attack/release, trim, time-stretch: no CC (docs by omission; ep-series-sysex: 'no CC maps to the 12 fader parameters')
Fader / punch-in FX 2.0 parameters (LVL, PTC, TIM, LPF, HPF, FX, ATK, REL, PAN, TUNE, VEL, MOD) and group FX send: no CC, not recordable over MIDI
FX type selection, tempo, swing, scene/pattern/project selection: no CC
Sound selection via program change / bank select CC 0/32: listed in the chart ('sounds 1-999') but not mapped since OS 2.0.2 (recorded/relayed only)

transport.notes: MIDI clock is OFF by default (code 100). SHIFT+ERASE then 101 = clock in (24 PPQN; the sequencer runs at 96 PPQN internally). Then Start/Stop/Continue/SPP from the Mac drive the sequencer. External START plays the cursor scene, and STOP chokes ringing one-shots. On internal clock the device ignores the Mac's START entirely (community). 102 = clock out. Song mode needs internal clock (SHIFT+PLAY on device). OS 2.5: SPP in song mode is relative to song start. 140/141 = reset controllers at stop off/on. The 3.5 mm SYNC jacks (codes 200-212) are separate from MIDI clock. Community: clock jitter about 0.12 ms, and about 140 note-ons in a burst on one song-mode start (cause open).

unsafeMessages: Any TE proprietary SysEx F0 00 20 76 33 ... (FILE protocol put/delete/metadata-set, project writes, 'switch to project', DFU firmware flashing). Can corrupt projects, wedge the file system until power-cycle, force a flash format (ERR CLOCK 43), or brick the unit (DFU). Never generate it. Only the universal identity request is safe.

Running any SysEx file session while TE's EP Sample Tool (or another tool) is connected: concurrent sessions freeze the device until power-cycle. Device debug frames F0 00 20 76 33 33 ... mean stop all SysEx.
Notes while the device is recording (REC armed / live record) are written into the pattern. Undo exists.
MIDI Start/Continue with clock-in (101) set starts the sequencer and plays the cursor scene. Stop chokes one-shots.
Program change + bank select (CC 0/32): no-op on OS >= 2.0.2, but switched sounds on OS 2.0-2.0.1. Avoid.
Note/CC floods: voice stealing drops notes (community lost 12-19 of 172 note-ons under voice pressure; polyphony 16 mono / 12 stereo voices).
MIDI thru (code 131) forwards input to MIDI out + USB. An app that echoes input to output creates a loop.
Not a MIDI message, but holding SHIFT+ERASE while powering on formats the device.

bestParameters: Note On 36-83 on channel 1: instant drum/pad hits across groups A-D (most reliable, about 3.6 ms)
MIDI clock + Start/Stop (after setting 101): the device's own pattern runs in sync (pad lights following the pattern is inferred)
CC 12 / CC 13: FX knob X/Y (e.g. FILTER cutoff/resonance) with the group's FX send up. OS >= 2.5, and verify first because one community test heard nothing
Per-pad channel (e.g. ch 2) + notes: play a bass/melody sample chromatically
demo.visualFeedback: No documented on-screen read-out of incoming CC values. Visible cues: the MIDI/USB icon appears when notes arrive (docs), pads light while their sounds play (inferred), and the sequencer display runs under external clock. CC 12/13 changes are mostly audible only.
demo.audibleFeedback: Pad triggers are immediate (community about 3.6 ms MIDI to USB audio). FX X/Y sweeps are only audible with an FX type selected and FX send > 0 on the playing group. Vibrato (CC 1) is subtle and needs a sustained KEY/LEGATO pad.
risks: Only 4 receivable CCs (1, 12, 13, 64), so it is a weak 'twist a knob' demo. Volume/pan/pitch/filter per pad are not MIDI-controllable.
CC 12/13 reported inaudible in one OS 2.5 hardware test. Rehearse on the actual unit and OS.
Default omni: notes 36-83 on any channel trigger pads (clashes with melodic channels).
Clock/start ignored unless code 101 is set on the device.
Never let generated code emit F0 00 20 76 ... SysEx.
setup: Confirm OS >= 2.5 on the device (identity reply shows zeros).
Load a project with drums on groups A/B. Select an FX (e.g. FILTER) and raise the FX send fader for that group.
Optional: SHIFT+ERASE 101 for clock in; SHIFT+ERASE 111 to stop omni clashes.
Close TE's EP Sample Tool before opening the app.
